History:
- Presenting complaint: Soreness, cracking, and dryness of the skin on the hands/fingers, primarily the palms; associated itching and occasional bleeding after scratching.
- Onset/duration: Symptoms began approximately 3–4 months ago.
- Progression/context: Gradual worsening, recently reached severity causing significant pain and impairment of work duties; off work for the past three days.
- Exposures/triggers: Works as a hotel housekeeper using cleaning products; recently changed jobs ~4 months ago; reports not consistently wearing gloves while cleaning.
- Associated symptoms: Mild generalized dry skin (legs); no fever, nausea, vomiting, bowel or urinary symptoms; appetite normal.
- Treatments tried: E45 emollient (no benefit); an oral antihistamine (no benefit).
- No prior diagnosis of eczema or dermatitis reported.

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Medications: Metformin — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: No known drug or other allergies.
- Family history: Family history of diabetes; no known family skin disease.
- Social: Works as a hotel housekeeper; inconsistent glove use while cleaning; does not smoke; drinks a couple of pints of alcohol per week.

Physical Examination:
- No formal vitals or clinician-performed exam findings documented in the transcript.
- Patient-reported/observed skin findings: cracked skin of palms/fingers, soreness, itching, occasional bleeding when scratched; no spontaneous bleeding reported.
- Relevant negatives from history: no fever, no systemic symptoms, no prior diagnosed skin conditions.

Impression:
- Clinical impression: Likely dermatitis, most consistent with contact dermatitis related to occupational exposure (cleaning products).

Management Plan:
- Advice: Avoid triggers; strongly advised to wear protective gloves when cleaning at all times.
- Topical therapy: Will prescribe a topical steroid cream — specific agent/dose/route/frequency not documented; prescription to be sent to the patient’s pharmacy.
- Emollients: Recommended application of stronger emollients, to be applied/“coated on” 3–4 times daily for the next couple of weeks.
- Follow-up: Return if no improvement after approximately 10–14 days, or sooner if symptoms worsen, spread, or cracking/dryness increases.
- Work: No formal work restriction documented; patient reported being off work for three days due to symptoms.

Patient Summary:
- Patient is a 45-year-old woman with 3–4 months of progressively painful, cracked, itchy palms after starting/working as a hotel housekeeper and inconsistent glove use. Likely occupational contact dermatitis.
- Plan: prescription topical steroid to be sent to pharmacy, intensified emollient use (3–4×/day), avoidance of triggers (gloves), and follow-up in 1–2 weeks if not improved or sooner if worsening.

Key Takeaways:
- Wear protective gloves for all cleaning tasks to avoid further exposure.
- Apply stronger emollients 3–4 times daily to restore skin hydration.
- Start prescribed topical steroid cream as directed (prescription to be sent); return earlier if symptoms worsen or spread.

Next Steps:
- Pharmacy: clinician to send prescription for topical steroid (agent and regimen to be clarified in prescription; not documented in transcript).
- Reassessment: clinical review in 10–14 days if inadequate response; earlier review if worsening.
- Consider escalation to alternative therapies or further investigation if no improvement at follow-up (no specific tests or referrals were ordered in the transcript).

- Internal conflicts from transcript: none substantive; minor unclear phrasing about leg dryness severity but no direct contradiction.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear and intelligible; intermittent brief interruptions and some incomplete fragments but sufficient for clinical history extraction.
